result.topic_en: Inversion of an Abel-type integral transform: if the integral of f(r)/sqrt(r^2-a^2) from a to infinity equals phi(a), then f is recovered from phi, proved by integrating a double integral over the plane in two ways; the page also gives the transform of a power r^{-n} via Gauss's Pi-function.
result.transcription:
Setzt man
$\int_a^\infty \frac{fr.\,\partial r}{\sqrt{(rr-aa)}} = \varphi a$ \qquad $\int_a^\infty \frac{r^{-n}.\,dr}{\sqrt{(rr-aa)}} = \frac{\Pi\frac12.\Pi(\frac12 n-1)}{\Pi(\frac12 n-\frac12)}.a^{-n}$
$\frac{d\varphi a}{da} = \varphi' a$ \qquad so wird
$2\int_a^\infty \frac{\varphi' r.\,da}{\pi.\sqrt{(rr-aa)}} = \frac{fa}{a}$
Also auch
$\frac{2d\int_a^\infty \frac{r\varphi r.\,\partial r}{\sqrt{(rr-aa)}}}{\pi da} = fa$
Der Beweis wird auf die doppelte Art
$\Omega = \iint_{-\infty\ -\infty}^{+\infty\ +\infty} \frac{fr}{r}.dx.dy$ \qquad wo $rr = hh+xx+yy$
zu integriren basirt
Die eine Integration gibt offenbar $\Omega = 2\pi\int_h^\infty fr.\partial r$
nach der andern [-gibt-] wenn man bei der ersten Integration $y$ als constant annimt
$\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \frac{fr\,dx}{r} = 2\int_0^\infty \frac{fr\,dx}{r} = 2\int_{\sqrt{([-hh+-]yy)}}^\infty \frac{fr.\,dr}{\sqrt{(rr-hh-yy)}}$
$= 2\varphi.\sqrt{(hh+yy)}$
Also die zweite
$2\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} \varphi(hh+yy).\,dy = 4\int_0^\infty \varphi\sqrt{(hh+yy)}.\,dy$
oder $hh+yy=\varrho\varrho$ gesetzt
$= 4\int \frac{\varrho\varphi\varrho.\,\partial\varrho}{\sqrt{(\varrho\varrho-hh)}}$. Es ist also $2\int \frac{\varrho\varphi\varrho.\,\partial\varrho}{\pi\sqrt{(\varrho\varrho-hh)}} = \int_h^\infty f\varrho\,\partial\varrho$
Ist also $Fz$ eine Function die für $z=\infty$ verschwindet und
deren derivirte $= -fz$ so ist $\int_h^\infty fr.\,dr = Fh$
also $-2\frac{d\int\frac{\varrho\varphi\varrho.\,\partial\varrho}{\pi\sqrt{(\varrho\varrho-hh)}}}{dh} = fh$ \quad W.Z.B.W

methods.what: Definition of the Abel-type transform phi of f
Transform of a power r^{-n} expressed with the Pi (factorial/Gamma) function
Inversion formula using the derivative of phi
Alternative inversion formula by differentiating an integral of r phi(r)
Proof by evaluating a planar double integral in two ways (polar coordinates vs iterated integration)
Polar evaluation of the double integral
Inner integral over x reduces to phi(sqrt(h^2+y^2))
Substitution h^2+y^2=rho^2 giving the identity relating integral of rho phi(rho) to integral of f
Final inversion by differentiation with respect to h

items.english: If phi is the transform of f, then 2/pi times the integral of phi'(r)/sqrt(r^2-a^2) from a to infinity equals f(a)/a.
Hence also: 2/pi times the derivative with respect to a of the integral of r phi(r)/sqrt(r^2-a^2) from a to infinity equals f(a).
